quote:
In the quiet after a ship’s breath, the hidden hand of illness reminds us that nature never warns us by lullabies.  

A promise of peace spoken in the roar of commerce may still ring with echoes of war; true ceasefire drips from gentler quiet.  

A cloak of authority, once draped upon a swift actor, sheds its weight only when the people finally breathe it out.  

Even the earth, when sealed, will quake at the feet of those who dare pry its secret; honor is the first stone of a proper closure.  

When a leader emerges from the shadows of confinement, his vessel may carry both the liberation of the weary and the remembrance of the past.  

The pain of a people can be a wound so deep that even the most subtle kindness must dig pieces from the rubble before the heart can heal.  

A garment fashioned from grain shows that the simplest of sustenance can ward off the frost of judgment like a humble cloak of wonder.
